text:
Ava: hit a reproducible stale-read during shard handoff. steps: client writes key K on node A, we start soft-evict/handshake to B, A serves a read that returns old value even after B applied the write.
Tom: can you sketch the timing? sounds like a race between write propagation and eviction visibility.
Ava: timeline: write -> ack on A (fast path), async replicate to B, handoff begins, A demotes but keeps serving from slab for a short window, B gets the write and becomes authoritative. subsequent read routed to A returns old value because A's slab wasn't updated and demote didn't mark slab unreadable.
Chen: is this different from the prefix-gen TOCTOU? feels related but more about replication+handoff ordering.
Ava: yep. gen fixes TOCTOU for demote itself, but here the problem is that ownership moves while in-flight replication completes. we need a correctness invariant: once ownership transfers to new node that has a later LSN for a key, old node must not serve older slabs for that key.
Maya: maybe we should add an ownership-epoch + last-known-lsn on the prefix. during handoff we bump epoch and tag the new owner with prefix.last_lsn = max(lsn_seen). readers check slab.lsn >= prefix.last_lsn before serving. if slab.lsn < prefix.last_lsn -> fallback/read-through.
Tom: interesting. detailed flow: on write to A we advance local LSN, replicate to B asynchronously. When B wins ownership, it will have seen the write via replication; but there is a window where ownership message arrives before replication does. need handshake to ensure new owner only becomes authoritative after it has applied or acknowledged up-to-date state for the prefix.
Chen: handshake options: (1) make ownership-change wait for replication to reach new owner (synchronous commit), (2) keep change fast and make old node fence reads until it's safe. choice affects latency.
Ava: (1) makes handoffs slow on popular prefixes. (2) complicates old-node logic but keeps majority of handoffs low-latency. we could hybrid: fast path if new owner confirms it has lsn >= meta.min_required_lsn, else queue a short-delay takeover.
Maya: propose token-based takeover: new owner requests a takeover token from current owner; current owner responds with token plus min_lsn it has flushed to stable storage. new owner waits until its lsn >= token.min_lsn then flips authoritative bit. meanwhile old owner marks prefix as "handoff_in_progress" and once it observes token issued it stops serving slabs with lsn < token.min_lsn.
Tom: nice. token carries (token_id, min_lsn, epoch). pseudocode for read path:
```
read_path(prefix, key) {
  if (prefix.handoff_in_progress) {
    if (slab.lsn(key) >= prefix.takeover_min_lsn) return slab.read(key);
    else return fallback_read(key);
  } else {
    return slab.read(key);
  }
}
```
Ava: how expensive is checking slab.lsn per-read? slab metadata needs to store LSN per entry anyway for GC/evict decisions; we can keep a compact u32 tag per entry.
Chen: metrics: count how many reads hit fallback during handoffs. if small we can accept. Also instrument handoff duration when token issued -> authoritative flip.
Maya: ops considerations: add top-level feature flag `runtime.flags.handoff_token_takeover` and a canary list. ops-bot: create playbook?
ops-bot: created #CANARY-919: "handoff-token takeover canary" assigned to @ava, due 2026-04-10 :white_check_mark:
Tom: corner cases: what if current owner is partitioned and never responds with token? new owner must be able to force takeover after timeout, but then clients might see stale reads until replication completes. we should choose timeout conservatively and log forced-takeovers.
Ava: plan: implement token handshake spike + microbench. default: fast takeover if new owner already has lsn >= required, else token + wait up to 200ms then force. Log forced cases as incidents.
Chen: testing: synthetic workload with high write fanout + frequent rebalances. chaos test: drop replication packets to simulate slowness.
Maya: also update guarantees docs: explain eventual takeover path and consistency window.
Ava: OK will open PR for spike, add metrics 'handoff.token_wait_ms' and 'handoff.fallback_reads'. ETA EOD Thursday with perf numbers.
Tom: thanks. this feels like the right balance between safety and not blocking rebalances.
Ava: thumbs up.
